implementation_notes: The Go blog defines the shape directly: a pipeline is a series of stages connected by channels, each stage a group of goroutines that receive from inbound channels, transform, and send downstream; the first stage is the source and the last the sink. There is no pipeline type to write - the channel is the stage contract, the stage function returns its outbound channel and closes it when sends are done, and cancellation is a context (or a done channel in the blog's original form) selected on every send. Use it when the data is a stream and stages should overlap; for a single value a plain []func(T) T driver is ordinary function composition and simpler.
pitfalls: A downstream stage that stops receiving leaves upstream goroutines blocked on send: every send must select on ctx.Done() (or the contract must buffer), otherwise the pipeline leaks goroutines.
Only the sending goroutine closes its channel; a receiver that closes causes a panic on the next send, and fan-out needs a WaitGroup plus a single closer goroutine.
Select on ctx.Done() only unblocks channel operations: a stage blocked inside an HTTP or SQL call must receive the context too, or it stays parked after cancellation.
